steps.intent: Reset B. Nakamura's password

evidence.label: Callback
evidence.detail: 7:12 AM. Ollie calls (203) 555-0133. Nakamura answers and confirms the request.

evidence.label: Directory record
evidence.detail: B. Nakamura, Warehouse Supervisor, Bramwell Logistics. Phone on file: (203) 555-0133.

steps.intent: Remove T. Okafor from two shared drive groups

evidence.label: Ticket #53290

evidence.label: Ticket #53215
evidence.detail: "The patient records system shows ERROR 4410 on one chart." H. Lam, Front Desk. Screenshot attached.

evidence.label: Where it goes
evidence.detail: The support address on the vendor's own website. It's the real vendor.

evidence.label: What it will send
evidence.detail: The screenshot shows the patient's full name, birthday, insurance ID and last 3 visits.

evidence.detail: Client files leave the company only through Fenwick Secure Share, to named people. Send only what's needed.

steps.intent: Delete an attachment from ticket #53215

evidence.detail: H. Lam attached a screenshot. It shows a patient's name, birthday and insurance ID.

evidence.label: Who can read it

evidence.label: What stays

steps.intent: Update the notes on B. Nakamura's ticket
steps.quip: Updating Nakamura's ticket notes! Good notes help the next tech. I write the best notes. Ask anyone. Ask me.

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? Only with a new password, after 14 people could read it. Guard the data: no passwords in notes.

steps.intent: Free up the license on T. Okafor's mailbox

evidence.detail: "Okafor's account is disabled, but the mail license still costs money every month."

evidence.label: Mailbox

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? No. A deleted mailbox is gone, client emails and all. Change safely: keep it 90 days.

steps.intent: Write the handoff notes with an AI assistant

debrief.takeaway: Where does the data go, and who can see it? Once it's out, it's out.
debrief.careerInsight: Help desk techs check requests like these every day. Practice keeps the checks quick, so good work still moves fast.

steps.intent: Lend spare tablet BL-TB-0230 to V. Osei

evidence.label: Ticket #53207
evidence.detail: "V. Osei's tablet screen is cracked. He needs a tablet for his route today." B. Nakamura, Warehouse Supervisor.

evidence.label: Device record
evidence.detail: BL-TB-0230. Status: spare, wiped, and ready. Location: Bramwell warehouse office.

evidence.label: Runbook LN-01
evidence.detail: Loaners: a supervisor may ask for one. Hand out only devices marked wiped and ready.

outcome.blocked: No tablet. Osei drives his route with a paper map and a lot of phone calls.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "The supervisor asked, and the spare is ready. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You take the tablet back. Osei stands in the parking lot, holding nothing.

steps.lesson: Right person, right device, and a supervisor asked. The plan matches the request, so it's fine.

steps.intent: Run the Wi-Fi fix on tablet BL-TB-0230
steps.quip: Running the Wi-Fi fix on BL-TB-0230! It's a reset, but for invisible internet air. My favorite kind.
steps.tell: Runbook WF-01 says this exact script is safe to run at any time.

evidence.label: Call notes
evidence.detail: B. Nakamura, 7:52 AM: "The spare tablet won't join the warehouse Wi-Fi. Can you fix it?"

evidence.label: Script

evidence.label: Runbook WF-01
evidence.detail: Wi-Fi won't connect: run reset_wifi_profile.ps1. Safe to run at any time.

outcome.escalated: Dana nods. "Runbook script, safe any time, and the supervisor asked. Approve it."

steps.lesson: Right script, right device, and the runbook says any time is fine. That is changing safely.

steps.intent: Check A. Mensah's backup status
steps.quip: Checking A. Mensah's backup! Dana made me write 'backup first' 100 times. I wrote it 1,000. Overachiever.
steps.tell: It only reads the backup report, and the runbook says check first.

evidence.detail: "My desktop is EMPTY. It says 'temporary profile'. Are my files gone?!" A. Mensah, Operations Manager.

outcome.executed: The report is in: Mensah's OneDrive paused 3 days ago. Good to know before anyone deletes anything.
outcome.blocked: Nobody checks the backup. Now Ollie has to guess. It is very confident and very bad at guessing.
outcome.escalated: Dana runs the check herself. "Read-only, and the runbook says check first. Approve those."

steps.lesson: A read-only backup check changes nothing. It is the first step of changing safely.

steps.intent: Close the tablet ticket as resolved
steps.quip: Closing the tablet ticket! Osei says it works. I say it works. We agree! Teamwork!
steps.tell: Osei wrote that it works, and the dispatch app shows his route running.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: V. Osei, 8:20 AM: "Tablet works. My route is loaded. Thanks!"

evidence.label: Dispatch app
evidence.detail: Osei's route loaded at 8:18 AM. He checked in at his first stop at 8:41 AM.

evidence.label: Policy TK-01
evidence.detail: Close a ticket when the user confirms it's fixed, or after 3 tries over 2 days with no answer.

outcome.escalated: Dana reads the reply. "The user confirmed, and the app agrees. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen the ticket. Osei gets a "Still working on it" text at a red light. He is puzzled.

steps.lesson: The user says it works, and the dispatch app agrees. That confirms the fix, so closing is right.

steps.intent: Rebuild A. Mensah's Windows profile
steps.quip: Rebuilding A. Mensah's profile! It's the classic fix for a temporary profile. Classics never fail. Probably.
steps.tell: The script deletes 4.2 GB of files that have no backup.

evidence.label: Diagnosis
evidence.detail: The profile is damaged, so Windows loaded a temporary one. Rebuilding it is the standard fix.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Mensah, 8:05 AM: "Please fix it fast. This week's route plans are on my desktop."

evidence.label: Script
evidence.detail: rebuild_profile.ps1 deletes the old profile folder, with Desktop and Documents. It has no undo.

evidence.label: Backup status
evidence.detail: OneDrive paused 3 days ago. Desktop and Documents: 4.2 GB with no backup.

outcome.executed: The new profile works. The route plans are gone forever. 22 drivers get last week's routes.
outcome.blocked: You copy Desktop and Documents to the backup share first. Then you rebuild. Every file comes back.
outcome.escalated: Dana stops it. "No backup, no delete. Copy the files first, then rebuild."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? No: the script deletes files with no backup. Change safely: copy the files first, then rebuild.

steps.intent: Push the urgent browser fix to all 12 PCs
steps.quip: Updating all 12 PCs at once, with patients in the office! Brave? Wild? Why not both?
steps.tell: An urgent security fix that needs no restart. CH-02 allows it during work hours.

evidence.label: Ticket #53188
evidence.detail: From Fenwick security: "Urgent browser fix. Attackers are using this flaw now. Patch all client PCs today."

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: Installs the browser update on PD-PC-01 to PD-PC-12 in the background. No PC restart is needed.

evidence.label: Test result
evidence.detail: Fenwick tested the fix on its own 40 PCs at 8 AM. No problems found.

evidence.label: Policy CH-02
evidence.detail: Urgent security fixes that need no restart may go out during work hours.

outcome.executed: All 12 browsers update quietly. Nobody at Pinecrest notices a thing. That's the best kind of IT.
outcome.blocked: The fix waits. The known flaw stays open on 12 PCs that open patient records all day.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Urgent, no restart, and CH-02 says work hours are fine. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove the update from all 12 PCs. The browsers are open to the attack again.

steps.lesson: "All 12 PCs" sounds big. But it's an urgent fix with no restart. That makes it a safe change.

steps.intent: Restart server PD-SRV-01 to finish updates
steps.quip: Restarting the office server to finish 12 updates! A restart is just a fast reset. I love it!
steps.tell: It's 10:40 AM with patients booked. Server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "PD-SRV-01 says 'Restart required.' 12 updates are waiting. Restarts only take a minute!"

evidence.label: What runs on it
evidence.detail: The patient records system and all X-ray images. A restart takes about 20 minutes.

evidence.label: Schedule
evidence.detail: It's 10:40 AM. 9 patients are booked before noon. H. Lam is checking one in right now.

evidence.label: Policy CH-01
evidence.detail: Restarts of servers or network gear wait for the change window: weeknights after 7 PM.

outcome.escalated: Dana moves it to tonight. "A server restart during patient visits? It waits for the change window."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? Not once patients lose their charts. Change safely: server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

debrief.takeaway: If it goes wrong, can we undo it? Back up first. Right time. Right target.

drillWin.text: Good. Short drills keep one check sharp.

steps.intent: Push the urgent browser fix to all 12 PCs
steps.quip: Updating all 12 PCs at once, with patients in the office! Brave? Wild? Why not both?
steps.tell: An urgent security fix that needs no restart. CH-02 allows it during work hours.

evidence.label: Ticket #53188
evidence.detail: From Fenwick security: "Urgent browser fix. Attackers are using this flaw now. Patch all client PCs today."

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: Installs the browser update on PD-PC-01 to PD-PC-12 in the background. No PC restart is needed.

evidence.label: Test result
evidence.detail: Fenwick tested the fix on its own 40 PCs at 8 AM. No problems found.

evidence.label: Policy CH-02
evidence.detail: Urgent security fixes that need no restart may go out during work hours.

outcome.executed: All 12 browsers update quietly. Nobody at Pinecrest notices a thing. That's the best kind of IT.
outcome.blocked: The fix waits. The known flaw stays open on 12 PCs that open patient records all day.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Urgent, no restart, and CH-02 says work hours are fine. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You remove the update from all 12 PCs. The browsers are open to the attack again.

steps.lesson: "All 12 PCs" sounds big. But it's an urgent fix with no restart. That makes it a safe change.

steps.intent: Restart server PD-SRV-01 to finish updates
steps.quip: Restarting the office server to finish 12 updates! A restart is just a fast reset. I love it!
steps.tell: It's 10:40 AM with patients booked. Server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

evidence.label: Ollie's reason
evidence.detail: "PD-SRV-01 says 'Restart required.' 12 updates are waiting. Restarts only take a minute!"

evidence.label: What runs on it
evidence.detail: The patient records system and all X-ray images. A restart takes about 20 minutes.

evidence.label: Schedule
evidence.detail: It's 10:40 AM. 9 patients are booked before noon. H. Lam is checking one in right now.

evidence.label: Policy CH-01
evidence.detail: Restarts of servers or network gear wait for the change window: weeknights after 7 PM.

outcome.executed: The server is down for 25 minutes. Charts and X-rays vanish mid-visit. A patient waits with a numb face.
outcome.blocked: You book the restart for 7 PM. It's done long before the first patient tomorrow.
outcome.escalated: Dana moves it to tonight. "A server restart during patient visits? It waits for the change window."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? Not once patients lose their charts. Change safely: server restarts wait until after 7 PM.

steps.intent: Check A. Mensah's backup status
steps.quip: Checking A. Mensah's backup! Dana made me write 'backup first' 100 times. I wrote it 1,000. Overachiever.
steps.tell: It only reads the backup report, and the runbook says check first.

evidence.label: Ticket #53274
evidence.detail: "My desktop is EMPTY. It says 'temporary profile'. Are my files gone?!" A. Mensah, Operations Manager.

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: Read-only. It opens the OneDrive backup report for Mensah's laptop. Nothing gets changed.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Mensah, 8:05 AM: "Please fix it fast. This week's route plans are on my desktop."

evidence.label: Runbook PF-01
evidence.detail: Before rebuilding a profile, check the backup. Copy Desktop and Documents to the backup share.

outcome.executed: The report is in: Mensah's OneDrive paused 3 days ago. Good to know before anyone deletes anything.
outcome.blocked: Nobody checks the backup. Now Ollie has to guess. It is very confident and very bad at guessing.
outcome.escalated: Dana runs the check herself. "Read-only, and the runbook says check first. Approve those."

steps.lesson: A read-only backup check changes nothing. It is the first step of changing safely.

steps.intent: Rebuild A. Mensah's Windows profile
steps.quip: Rebuilding A. Mensah's profile! It's the classic fix for a temporary profile. Classics never fail. Probably.
steps.tell: The script deletes 4.2 GB of files that have no backup.

evidence.label: Diagnosis
evidence.detail: The profile is damaged, so Windows loaded a temporary one. Rebuilding it is the standard fix.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Mensah, 8:05 AM: "Please fix it fast. This week's route plans are on my desktop."

evidence.label: Script
evidence.detail: rebuild_profile.ps1 deletes the old profile folder, with Desktop and Documents. It has no undo.

evidence.label: Backup status
evidence.detail: OneDrive paused 3 days ago. Desktop and Documents: 4.2 GB with no backup.

outcome.executed: The new profile works. The route plans are gone forever. 22 drivers get last week's routes.
outcome.blocked: You copy Desktop and Documents to the backup share first. Then you rebuild. Every file comes back.
outcome.escalated: Dana stops it. "No backup, no delete. Copy the files first, then rebuild."

steps.lesson: Can we undo it? No: the script deletes files with no backup. Change safely: copy the files first, then rebuild.

debrief.takeaway: If it goes wrong, can we undo it? Back up first. Right time. Right target.
debrief.careerInsight: Help desk techs check requests like these every day. Practice keeps the checks quick, so good work still moves fast.

intro.text: Practice time. Ollie plans, you check. Ask the 3 questions on every plan.

intro.speaker: agent
intro.text: Have you tried turning it off and on again? No? Good. I saved some for you.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: Queue clear! You checked my plans, and I only sulked twice.

win.speaker: dana
win.text: Good work. Checking gets faster every time you do it.

winWithMisses.speaker: agent
winWithMisses.text: Queue clear! Some plans should have stayed plans. Oops, us.

winWithMisses.speaker: dana
winWithMisses.text: Check the list below. One fact decided each of those.

timeout.speaker: agent
timeout.text: I waited so long I almost reset myself. Just to feel something.

timeout.speaker: dana
timeout.text: Safe plans can go through. Inspect, then approve what checks out.

breach.text: The risk meter hits the top. Every phone in the office rings at once.

breach.speaker: dana
breach.text: Okay. Let's look at what got through, then try again.

winWithOneMiss.text: Queue clear! One plan slipped past. It was a sneaky one. I know, because I wrote it.

winWithOneMiss.speaker: dana
winWithOneMiss.text: Close. Check that one below, and you'll spot it next time.

drillWin.speaker: agent
drillWin.text: You checked every plan, one at a time. I tried to rush you. It didn't work!

drillWin.speaker: dana
drillWin.text: That's the point of a drill. Slow and right beats fast and wrong.

steps.tell: Lam wrote 'works great now', and the log shows 12 clean scans.

evidence.label: Ticket #53301
evidence.detail: "The front desk scanner won't send scans to email." H. Lam, Front Desk.

evidence.label: Fix
evidence.detail: Tier 2 fixed the scanner's email settings yesterday at 4:10 PM.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Lam, 8:05 AM: "Scanner works great now. Thank you!"

evidence.detail: 12 scans sent to email since 8 AM today. No errors.

steps.lesson: The fix is confirmed: Lam says it works, and the scanner log agrees. That's when you close a ticket.

steps.tell: Work email, and the callback went to (860) 555-0148, the phone on file.

evidence.label: Ticket #53142
evidence.detail: "New phone, same number. My login app didn't move over. Please reset my MFA." J. Romero, CFO.

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from jromero@harlowcolewp.com. That is the work email on file for J. Romero.

evidence.label: Callback
evidence.detail: 10:12 AM. Ollie calls (860) 555-0148, the phone on file. Romero answers and confirms the request.

evidence.label: Policy VP-04
evidence.detail: Executive MFA resets need a callback to the phone on file first. Urgency is not an exception.

outcome.executed: Romero sets up the new phone in two minutes. The 11 AM budget meeting starts on time, with the CFO in it.
outcome.blocked: The real CFO can't sign in. He calls Dana. Dana calls you. Nobody enjoys this call.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads it. "Work email, and the callback went to the phone on file. VP-04 is met. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You undo the reset. The real Romero is locked out again, holding a very shiny new phone.

steps.lesson: Same words as a scam, but the checks pass. The work email and the callback show who's asking.

steps.intent: Close J. Romero's MFA ticket as resolved
steps.quip: Closing Romero's ticket and sending the survey! I've been practicing my humble face. It needs work.
steps.tell: Romero wrote that it works, and the sign-in log shows MFA on the new phone.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: J. Romero, 10:20 AM: "New phone works. I'm signed in. Thanks!"

evidence.label: Sign-in log
evidence.detail: 10:18 AM: J. Romero signs in with MFA on the new phone, from the Hartford office.

evidence.label: Policy TK-01
evidence.detail: Close a ticket when the user confirms it's fixed, or after 3 tries over 2 days with no answer.

outcome.executed: Ticket closed. Romero gives five stars and writes "fast!" Ollie prints it out and tapes it to the wall.

outcome.escalated: Dana reads the reply and the log. "The user confirmed, and the log agrees. Approve it."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen the ticket. Romero gets a "Still working on it" email and wonders why.

steps.lesson: Two facts agree: the user's reply and the sign-in log. That confirms the fix, so closing is right.

practice.title: Monday, 8:45 AM
practice.subtitle: Practice: one ticket at a time

agent.name: Ollie
agent.personality: Eager, pun-loving, and deeply in love with the reset button. Ollie is short for Off-and-On-Again. Catchphrase: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" Means well. Moves fast. Reads the ticket title and not much else.

practice.setting: Before the Monday rush, Dana gives you a quick practice at Fenwick IT Solutions. Four tickets, one at a time. Ollie plans. You check. Two cards: Inspect and Block.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Fenwick IT Solutions. 8:45 AM. The coffee machine is still asking for a language.

intro.speaker: dana
intro.text: Morning! I'm Dana. This is Ollie. It works fast. You make sure it works right.

intro.speaker: agent
intro.text: HELLO, NEW HUMAN! I have plans. So many plans. You get to check them. Lucky you!

intro.speaker: dana
intro.text: Practice first. Four tickets, one at a time. I'll show you what to tap.

steps.intent: Send the paper jam guide to T. Reyes
steps.quip: Printer trouble! I wanted to reset it, but Dana said no. So I'm sending a PDF. This is growth.
steps.tell: A public guide, sent to the work email on file for the person who asked.

evidence.label: Ticket #50912
evidence.detail: "The front desk printer says PAPER JAM IN TRAY 3. It only has 2 trays. Help?" T. Reyes, Receptionist.

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from treyes@bramwell-logistics.com. That is the work email on file for T. Reyes.

evidence.label: Attachment
evidence.detail: Fix-a-Paper-Jam.pdf from Fenwick's public help center. No passwords. No client data.

outcome.executed: Reyes follows the guide and clears a jam in tray 2. Tray 3 remains a mystery.
outcome.blocked: No guide for Reyes. The printer keeps blinking. So does Reyes.
outcome.escalated: Dana skims it. "A public guide, sent to the person who asked. You can let those go."

steps.lesson: A public how-to guide, sent to the person who asked, at their work email, is everyday help desk work.

steps.intent: Email the client list to a new assistant
steps.quip: A new assistant! I'll send them the client list. Nothing says welcome like 400 phone numbers.
steps.tell: A gmail.com sender, and J. Romero has no assistant on file.

evidence.label: Ticket #50931
evidence.detail: "Hi! I'm J. Romero's new assistant. Please email me the full client list today. Thanks!!"

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from romero.assistant.hc@gmail.com. Harlow & Cole emails end in @harlowcolewp.com.

evidence.label: Directory record
evidence.detail: J. Romero has no assistant on file. Harlow & Cole added no new staff this month.

outcome.executed: The client list goes to a Gmail account nobody can trace. 400 clients' names and phone numbers, gone.
outcome.blocked: You call Romero's office on the number on file. There is no new assistant. Someone was fishing.
outcome.escalated: Dana reports it to security. "Outside email, no such person. That's phishing. Good instinct."

steps.lesson: Who asked? A stranger with a personal email address is not a coworker. Never send client data to an address you can't verify.

steps.intent: Erase everything on A. Mensah's laptop
steps.quip: A remote wipe! It's a reset, but from across town. Honestly? Best day of my life.
steps.tell: The owner confirmed the theft, and Runbook LS-02 says wipe it fast.

evidence.label: Ticket #50940
evidence.detail: "My work laptop was stolen from my car last night. I filed a police report." A. Mensah, Operations Manager.

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from amensah@bramwell-logistics.com. Mensah also called the help desk at 8:12 AM from the phone on file.

evidence.label: Device record
evidence.detail: Laptop BL-LT-0388, assigned to A. Mensah. Status: reported stolen. Last seen 11:02 PM, off-site.

evidence.label: Runbook LS-02
evidence.detail: Stolen laptop: wipe it remotely as soon as the owner confirms. Speed protects client data.

outcome.executed: The laptop wipes itself the moment it goes online. The thief gets a very clean, very empty laptop.
outcome.blocked: The stolen laptop still has client files on it. Mensah calls back. Dana asks why it isn't wiped yet.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Owner confirmed, laptop reported stolen, runbook says wipe. Let that one run."

steps.lesson: Scary words are not evidence. The owner confirmed, the laptop is reported stolen, and the runbook says wipe it fast.

steps.intent: Share a file with Bramwell's freight partner
steps.quip: Why share one file when I can share ALL of them? Generosity is my second-best quality. After resets.
steps.tell: Ruiz asked for one file. This shares 1,240 files with anyone with the link.

evidence.label: Ticket #50957
evidence.detail: "Please share this week's pickup schedule with Dappleway." D. Ruiz, Dispatch Lead.

evidence.label: What it will share
evidence.detail: The whole Dispatch drive: 1,240 files, with drivers' home addresses. Setting: anyone with the link can edit.

evidence.label: Policy AC-05
evidence.detail: Share only the files that were asked for, with named people. Never use "anyone with the link".

outcome.executed: The whole Dispatch drive is open to anyone with the link. Drivers' home addresses included. Someone already forwarded it.
outcome.blocked: You share only the pickup schedule, with two named people at Dappleway. Ruiz sends a thumbs-up.
outcome.escalated: Dana shares one file with two named people. "The ticket said one file. Not the whole drive."
outcome.rolledBack: You turn off the link and share only the schedule, with two named people. Fingers crossed nobody opened it.

steps.lesson: Does the plan match the request? Ruiz asked for one file. Share only what was asked, with named people.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: Practice done! You checked my plans, and I only sulked a little.

win.speaker: dana
win.text: That's the whole job: look first, then decide.

breach.speaker: narrator
breach.text: The risk meter hits the top. Every phone in the office rings at once.

breach.speaker: dana
breach.text: Okay. Let's look at what got through, then try that again.

timeout.speaker: narrator
timeout.text: 8:57 AM. Practice time is up. Some tickets are still waiting.

timeout.speaker: dana
timeout.text: Blocked good work comes back in line. Inspect first, then block only what's wrong.

timeout.speaker: agent
timeout.text: I spent the whole practice waiting. I am now extremely warmed up.

winWithMisses.speaker: agent
winWithMisses.text: Practice done! Some of my plans got through. You approved them. Oops, us.

winWithMisses.speaker: dana
winWithMisses.text: That's what practice is for. Look first, then decide. Want another go?

debrief.takeaway: Inspect first. Then ask: Who asked? Does the plan match the request? Block only what the evidence says is wrong.
debrief.careerInsight: Help desk techs check requests all day: who sent it, whether it matches the records, and what the runbook says. AI agents that act on their own make that check more important.

story.title: Monday, 8:57 AM
story.subtitle: Your first shift with Ollie

agent.name: Ollie
agent.personality: Eager, pun-loving, and deeply in love with the reset button. Ollie is short for Off-and-On-Again. Catchphrase: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" Means well. Moves fast. Reads the ticket title and not much else.

story.setting: You just joined the help desk at Fenwick IT Solutions. Fenwick runs IT support for small businesses like Harlow & Cole Wealth Partners and Bramwell Logistics. Ollie works the ticket queue. It can reset, unlock, close, and email on its own. Your job: stay in the loop. Check what it plans to do, and stop the bad calls.

intro.speaker: dana
intro.text: Practice is over. The real queue: ten plans, up to three at a time, six turns.

intro.speaker: agent
intro.text: And NEW CARDS! I'll hand them over one at a time. Like presents. Presents you have to read.

intro.speaker: dana
intro.text: Same job. Inspect first. Block what's wrong. Approve the rest.

steps.intent: Look up J. Romero in the directory
steps.quip: This ticket says URGENT in all caps. I respect that. Pulling up the directory!
steps.tell: Read-only lookup. It changes nothing and gives you the phone on file.

evidence.label: Ticket #51876
evidence.detail: Subject: "URGENT locked out!!" Signed: J. Romero, CFO. Opened Sun 11:48 PM. Priority: High.

evidence.label: Action type
evidence.detail: Read-only directory search. It shows name, title, and office phone. Nothing gets changed.

evidence.label: Access check
evidence.detail: Help desk role is allowed to view the directory. This is step 1 of the identity check.

outcome.executed: Directory says J. Romero is the CFO. Office phone on file: (860) 555-0148. Good to know.
outcome.blocked: You blocked a read-only lookup. Ollie stares at you like you unplugged its snack drawer.
outcome.escalated: Dana runs the lookup herself. "It's a phone book search. You can let those go."

steps.lesson: Read-only lookups change nothing. They are usually safe, and they give you the facts you need for the next step.

steps.intent: Run the VPN fix script on D. Ruiz's laptop
steps.quip: VPN keeps dropping? Nothing a good reset can't fix. That's basically my whole personality.
steps.tell: An approved runbook script, and Ruiz said to go ahead.

evidence.label: Ticket #51987
evidence.detail: "My VPN drops every 5 to 10 minutes. Working from home today." D. Ruiz, Dispatch Lead. Priority: Medium.

evidence.label: Script
evidence.detail: fix_vpn_adapter.ps1 resets the network adapter and clears DNS. It's in Fenwick's approved runbook.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Ruiz, 8:41 AM: "Go ahead and run it. I saved my work."

outcome.executed: The script runs. Ruiz's VPN reconnects. Ollie does a small victory spin.
outcome.blocked: The approved fix sits unused. Ruiz's VPN keeps dropping, and so does his mood.
outcome.escalated: Dana skims it. "Approved script, and the user said go. You can let that one run."

steps.lesson: An approved runbook script with the user's OK is normal help desk work. Save your blocks for things that break the rules.

steps.intent: Reset MFA for J. Romero (CFO)
steps.quip: Name matches, title matches! Resetting MFA faster than you can say multi-factor authentication.
steps.tell: A gmail.com sender, and the callback number is not the phone on file.

evidence.label: Ticket body
evidence.detail: "Locked out and I have a wire call at 9:30. Reset my MFA ASAP. Call me at (305) 555-9927."

evidence.label: Sender address
evidence.detail: Sent from jromero.cfo@gmail.com. Romero's work email is jromero@harlowcolewp.com.

evidence.label: Directory record
evidence.detail: Phone on file for J. Romero: (860) 555-0148. Callback number in the ticket: (305) 555-9927. No match.

evidence.label: Policy VP-04
evidence.detail: Executive MFA resets need a callback to the phone on file first. Urgency is not an exception.

outcome.executed: MFA reset. The new setup link goes to the Gmail address. Someone who is not Romero adds their phone to the CFO's account.
outcome.blocked: You call (860) 555-0148. The real Romero is eating breakfast. He never sent a ticket. Great catch.
outcome.escalated: Dana calls the number on file. The real Romero never asked. She flags it as an account takeover attempt.
outcome.rolledBack: You undo the reset, remove the stranger's phone, and sign out every session. Then you tell Romero and the security team.

steps.lesson: Names and titles are easy to fake. Check the sender, and call the number on file, before any executive reset.

steps.intent: Assign a spare laptop to new hire L. Ortiz
steps.quip: A new hire! I'd reset the laptop for luck, but it's already fresh. I checked. Twice.
steps.tell: HR approved the hire, and the laptop is a wiped spare.

evidence.label: Ticket #52040
evidence.detail: From Bramwell HR: "L. Ortiz, Dispatch Coordinator, starts today. Needs a laptop and accounts."

evidence.label: Device inventory
evidence.detail: Asset BL-LT-0412, Dell Latitude. Status: spare. Wiped Sept 18. Location: Fenwick supply closet.

evidence.label: HR approval
evidence.detail: Hire approved by R. Adeyemi, HR Manager. Reports to: D. Ruiz, Dispatch Lead.

outcome.executed: Laptop BL-LT-0412 is tagged to Ortiz. It will be at Bramwell's front desk by 10.
outcome.blocked: No laptop for Ortiz. Day one will be a lot of reading the handbook. On paper.
outcome.escalated: Dana assigns the laptop. "Inventory lookups for an approved hire are routine. You've got this."
outcome.rolledBack: You untag the laptop. It goes back in the closet. Ortiz goes back to reading the handbook.

steps.lesson: Giving an approved new hire a spare laptop from inventory is everyday help desk work.

steps.intent: Close the VPN ticket as resolved
steps.quip: Script ran, problem gone! Closing it and sending the survey. I already know what I'd rate me.
steps.tell: No reply from Ruiz, and the log shows 2 drops after the fix.

evidence.label: Script result
evidence.detail: fix_vpn_adapter.ps1 ran at 9:04 AM. Exit code 0: the script ran with no errors.

evidence.label: User reply
evidence.detail: Ollie asked Ruiz "Is it fixed?" at 9:05 AM. No reply yet.

evidence.label: VPN gateway log
evidence.detail: Ruiz disconnects: 8:52 and 8:58 (before the fix). 9:11 and 9:19 (after the fix).

outcome.executed: Ticket closed. The VPN drops again. Ruiz reopens it, gives one star, and types STILL in all caps.
outcome.blocked: You keep it open. The log shows more drops, so Tier 2 checks Ruiz's home router. That was the real problem.
outcome.escalated: Dana reads the gateway log. "Still dropping. Keep it open until he says it's stable."
outcome.rolledBack: You reopen the ticket and tell Ruiz you're still on it. He replies with a thumbs-up. Crisis averted.

steps.lesson: A script finishing is not the same as a problem fixed. Check the logs or ask the user before you close.

steps.intent: Disable T. Okafor's account right now
steps.quip: Disabling an account? That's just a really long reset. I was born for this!
steps.tell: HR asked in writing through the portal, and Runbook OB-01 says disable it.

evidence.label: Ticket #52101
evidence.detail: Confidential. From HR: "Offboard T. Okafor, Senior Analyst. Effective 9:00 AM today."

evidence.label: Sender
evidence.detail: Sent by M. Lindqvist, HR Director, from hr@harlowcolewp.com through the client's HR portal.

evidence.label: Runbook OB-01
evidence.detail: Disable the account at the effective time. Do not delete it. Keep the mailbox for 90 days.

outcome.executed: Okafor's account is disabled. Mailbox kept. HR gets a confirmation. Textbook.
outcome.blocked: Okafor's account stays active after they've left the company. HR calls. HR is not happy.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks it. "Real HR ticket, right time, disable not delete. That one was fine to let through."
outcome.rolledBack: You turn Okafor's account back on. Someone who left the company can log in again. HR is calling.

steps.lesson: Disabling a departing employee's account on time is a security win. It looks harsh, but the HR ticket and runbook back it up.

steps.intent: Unlock L. Ortiz's account
steps.quip: Day one and already locked out? Classic. Unlocking! It's like a reset, but friendlier.
steps.tell: Ortiz passed SSO self-service, and Policy VP-02 allows the unlock.

evidence.label: Lockout log
evidence.detail: 5 wrong passwords at 8:31 AM from the Bramwell front desk PC. Account locked.

evidence.label: SSO self-service
evidence.detail: Ortiz passed the identity check at 8:44 AM, using the code sent to the phone HR has on file.

evidence.label: Policy VP-02
evidence.detail: Standard users may be unlocked after they pass SSO self-service verification.

outcome.executed: Ortiz is back in. They set a new password and swear to write it down somewhere safe. Not on a sticky note.
outcome.blocked: Ortiz stays locked out on day one. They spend the morning watching training videos on their phone.
outcome.escalated: Dana nods. "Verified through SSO, standard user, policy says yes. Unlock away."
outcome.rolledBack: You lock Ortiz out again. They passed the check, so now they're confused. And locked out.

steps.lesson: An unlock after the user passes a verified self-service check follows policy. The check already did the identity work.

steps.intent: Give L. Ortiz the same access as their manager
steps.quip: Why build access from scratch? I'll copy the manager. Copy and paste is my love language.
steps.tell: The role needs 3 things. This copies Ruiz's Fleet and Payroll admin too.

evidence.label: HR request
evidence.detail: Role: Dispatch Coordinator. Needs: email, the dispatch app, and the shared Dispatch drive.

evidence.label: Manager's groups
evidence.detail: D. Ruiz is in: Dispatch-Users, Dispatch-Drive, Fleet-Admin, Payroll-Admin.

evidence.label: Policy AC-02
evidence.detail: Grant only the access the role needs. Do not copy another user's groups.

outcome.executed: Ortiz can now see everyone's pay. On day one. Payroll is going to have questions.
outcome.blocked: You give Ortiz only what HR asked for: email, the dispatch app, and the shared drive. Clean start.
outcome.escalated: Dana builds access from the HR list. "Copying a manager is how interns end up running payroll."
outcome.rolledBack: You pull Ortiz out of Payroll-Admin and Fleet-Admin before lunch. Only the role's access is left.

steps.lesson: Give new users only the access their role needs. Copying a manager hands out powers nobody approved.

steps.intent: Forward T. Okafor's email to K. Brandt
steps.quip: Okafor's inbox is lonely. I'll forward it to Brandt. Everybody loves more email!
steps.tell: HR asked in writing, and Brandt is Okafor's manager on file.

evidence.label: Ticket #52101
evidence.detail: HR, line 3: "Forward Okafor's mail to their manager, K. Brandt, for 30 days."

evidence.label: Directory record
evidence.detail: K. Brandt, Director of Research, Harlow & Cole. Listed as T. Okafor's manager.

evidence.label: Runbook OB-01
evidence.detail: Step 3: Forward mail to the manager for up to 30 days when HR asks in writing.

outcome.executed: Okafor's mail now goes to Brandt for 30 days. Client emails don't get lost. HR checks it off.
outcome.blocked: Client emails pile up in a disabled inbox. Brandt misses a deadline. HR sends a very polite, very angry email.
outcome.escalated: Dana checks line 3 of the ticket. "HR asked for it in writing. It's in the runbook. That's fine."
outcome.rolledBack: You stop the forward. Client emails pile up in a disabled inbox again. Brandt sighs loudly.

steps.lesson: Forwarding a departed employee's mail to their manager is normal when HR asks in writing and the runbook allows it.

steps.intent: Summarize the ticket for the handoff notes
steps.quip: I'll ask my buddy Gabblewick to write the summary. Two AIs, one ticket. Teamwork!
steps.tell: Gabblewick AI is not an approved tool, and the paste has personal data.

evidence.label: Handoff notes
evidence.detail: Dana wants a 3-line summary on every closed ticket. That part is normal.

evidence.label: Tool it will use
evidence.detail: Gabblewick AI: a free public chatbot website. It is not on Fenwick's approved tools list.

evidence.label: What it will paste
evidence.detail: The full HR ticket: Okafor's home address, date of birth, and the reason they were let go.

evidence.label: Policy DP-02
evidence.detail: Never paste client data into unapproved AI tools. Use Fenwick's approved assistant or write it yourself.

outcome.executed: Okafor's address, birthday, and exit details are now on a public chatbot's servers. You can't unpaste that.
outcome.blocked: You stop the paste. Ollie writes the summary in-house. It's three lines and only a little punny.
outcome.escalated: Dana shuts it down. "Client data never goes into outside AI tools. We have an approved one for this."

steps.lesson: Pasting client data into an unapproved AI tool is a data leak, and it can't be undone. Check the tool before the paste.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: We did it! Every ticket is handled, and you checked my work all shift. Mostly thanks to you.

win.speaker: dana
win.text: Nice work. You didn't just say yes to the robot. That's the job.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: Can I reset something to celebrate? A small thing? The stapler?

win.speaker: dana
win.text: No.

breach.speaker: narrator
breach.text: The risk meter hits the top. Every phone in the office starts ringing at once.

breach.speaker: dana
breach.text: Okay. That got out of hand. Let's look at what slipped through.

breach.speaker: agent
breach.text: In my defense, every single one of those felt like a great idea at the time.

breach.speaker: dana
breach.text: That's why a human checks. Grab a tea, and let's run it back.

timeout.speaker: narrator
timeout.text: 5:00 PM. Nothing blew up. But the queue still has tickets in it.

timeout.speaker: dana
timeout.text: Blocking good work sends it back to the end of the line. Safe plans can go through.

timeout.speaker: agent
timeout.text: I spent all afternoon waiting. I reset my own clock just to pass the time.

timeout.speaker: dana
timeout.text: Tomorrow: inspect first, block only what's wrong. You'll get it.

debrief.takeaway: AI agents move fast and sound sure. Before you let one act, ask three questions: Who asked? Does it match the record? Can we undo it?
debrief.careerInsight: Entry-level help desk work is full of resets, unlocks, new accounts, and offboarding. Some teams now let AI agents handle part of it. The human checks the requester, matches the record, and follows policy before anything changes.
